classification.difficultyReason: Calculate cylindrical and rectangular container volumes and justify whether the transferred water fits.

inlines.text: Marta fills the cylindrical container with water.
She then pours the water into the rectangular prism-shaped container.
Will all of the water fit into the rectangular prism?
Justify your answer with mathematical reasoning.

spec.description: Upright cylindrical container, diameter 10 cm above and height 11 cm at left.
spec.mathematics: Cylinder radius 5 cm and height 11 cm. Camera above the top rim; top ellipse complete, vertical boundaries are silhouettes, bottom front arc visible. Source omits the hidden rear bottom arc.

spec.description: Tall rectangular prism-shaped container with base dimensions 6 cm and 7 cm and height 12 cm.
spec.mathematics: Rectangular prism with perpendicular base lengths 6 and 7 cm, height 12 cm. Projection basis for its unit box: u=(0.95,0.16), v=(-0.6,0.18), w=(0,2.15). Camera toward negative u, negative v and positive w. Visible faces u=0, v=0 and w=1. Source omits concealed edges.

answer.short: No. The cylinder holds $275\pi\,\mathrm{cm}^3\approx863.94\,\mathrm{cm}^3$, but the prism holds only $504\,\mathrm{cm}^3$.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}r&=\frac{10}{2}=5\,\mathrm{cm}\\V_{\mathrm{cylinder}}&=\pi r^2h\\V_{\mathrm{cylinder}}&=\pi\times5^2\times11\\V_{\mathrm{cylinder}}&=275\pi\,\mathrm{cm}^3\\V_{\mathrm{cylinder}}&\approx863.94\,\mathrm{cm}^3\\V_{\mathrm{prism}}&=Ah\\V_{\mathrm{prism}}&=(6\times7)\times12\\V_{\mathrm{prism}}&=504\,\mathrm{cm}^3\end{align*}$$ No. Since $275\pi>504$, the water will not all fit.
